message: Can you look at this ECG? I think it's normal, right?
reply:
**I wouldn’t call this ECG normal.** From the image, the rhythm looks irregular, with no clearly consistent P waves and a heart rate around **130 beats/minute**. That is concerning for **atrial fibrillation with a fast ventricular rate**, though a clinician needs to confirm it from the original tracing. An irregular rhythm without distinct P waves is characteristic of atrial fibrillation. [Merck Manual](https://www.merckmanuals.com/professional/cardiovascular-disorders/overview-of-arrhythmias-and-conduction-disorders/overview-of-arrhythmias)

There are also prominent chest-lead voltages and some ST–T changes that need clinical review. A photo alone cannot establish their cause or rule out a heart attack.

**If this is your current ECG, arrange medical assessment today**, especially if this rhythm is new. If you have chest pain, shortness of breath, fainting, or severe dizziness, seek emergency care now.

When was this recorded, and are you having any symptoms or a known history of atrial fibrillation?
